title: Reading his birth certificate: Springfield, Ohio, 1918, parents listed as colored
summary: Thompson reads details from his birth certificate: birth date, parents Jesse and Laura Thompson, race, occupations, and the death of his mother when he was five.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So I would like to start out by saying that to my knowledge, which is illegal from my birth certificate, which I'm holding in my hand now, and it's listed as coming from the County of Clark, I believe it says here, from the State of Ohio, bureau of vital statistics, certificate of birth, which has to do with who I am. Sir Charles, who is Sir Charles Thompson? And the file number of this seems to be 21322 with a possible writing of 8 in there someplace. These papers are not always exactly clear. Some of the writing. Registration district number 175, primary registra-
tion district 8073, registration number 345. That should be enough information from that to identify this paper from the vital statistics bureau.

And my birth place was Springfield, Ohio, and my place of residence, the residence of my parents was 361 Henzo Avenue, and my full name is Charles Philip Walker Thompson, which I believe most of those names were named after people in my family who were either ministers or physicians perhaps. At least I know that one of them was a minister in the family beside my father, I believe it was on the Walker side, which is my mother. And my birth date was March the 21st, 1918. My father was Jesse L. Thompson, and my mother was Laura Walker Thompson.

And on the birth certificate which is very significant at this time of this interview, May the 5th,1975, my father is listed, his race as colored, c-o-l-o-r-e-d, something I would like to discuss in this interview. And his age was 41, my mother was also listed as colored, aged 38. My father's birth place and my mother's birth place was Mount Sterling, Kentucky. My father's occupation in industry was listed as minister, my mother's occupation in industry was interestingly enough listed as domestic. I guess that means that she took care of us because I don't remember whether she had a job or not, because She died when I was five years old, my mother, my real mother died when I was five years old. My father married again
